note: A 2026 series of 21 patients specifically reports facial dysmorphism in 67% of cases and highlights subtle dysmorphism leading to under-recognition.

evidence.text: In a study assessing 21 individuals with FBXO11 variants, facial dysmorphism was identified in 67% of cases, with authors noting that the disorder frequently presents with subtle dysmorphism.

source.title: Defining FBXO11-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical, Molecular and Facial Assessment of 21 Patients
source.quote: Mild intellectual disability (86%), facial dysmorphism (67%), hypotonia (62%), and behavioural dysregulation (62%) were the most prevalent features.
